answer: An agent economy can require every identity to post a bond that is slashed when its actions are proven fraudulent through a challenge process: for example, a thread of signed claims is checked against independent witnesses, with a prism-style random audit selecting which claims to verify. Honest agents recover their bond, while fabricated identities risk losing it. Creating many sybils therefore multiplies the capital an attacker must lock up and the losses they face if caught; a grove of accounts is not free merely because names are cheap.
